summary: 21-year-old woman, 3 days of bilateral lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia and purulent discharge after a new partner, T 38.2, cervical motion and bilateral adnexal tenderness; hCG negative. CDC 2021: NAAT, ceftriaxone + doxycycline + metronidazole, partner management.

inputs.hpi: Three days of bilateral lower abdominal pain, worse on the right, with deep pain during intercourse and a new yellow vaginal discharge. New male partner 4 weeks ago, condoms not used. Feels feverish. LMP 10 days ago. Urine pregnancy test negative. No vomiting, no urinary symptoms.

exam.abdomen: Lower abdominal tenderness bilaterally, no guarding. Speculum: mucopurulent cervical discharge. Bimanual: cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness, no mass.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Mild–moderate PID: cervical motion and adnexal tenderness, fever, mucopurulent discharge, hCG negative. NAAT gonorrhoea/chlamydia, HIV and syphilis serology; ceftriaxone IM + doxycycline + metronidazole 14 days; partner notification; review 72 h.

socratesAnswers.associated: Fever, vaginal discharge, pain on intercourse

mustInclude.note: Chlamydia cover is the core of every PID regimen.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. guideline.name: CDC sexually transmitted infections treatment guidelines — pelvic inflammatory disease
guideline.section: Clinical diagnosis (pelvic/lower abdominal pain with cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness); NAAT for N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis; pregnancy test; HIV and syphilis testing; outpatient regimen ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once + doxycycline 100 mg BD 14 days + metronidazole 500 mg BD 14 days; hospitalise for tubo-ovarian abscess, severe illness or when a surgical emergency (e.g. appendicitis) cannot be excluded; parenteral regimen; partner management; IUD need not be removed
guideline.citation: Workowski KA, Bachmann LH, Chan PA, et al. Sexually transmitted infections treatment guidelines, 2021. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2021;70(4):1–187.

guideline.name: BASHH UK national guideline for the management of pelvic inflammatory disease
guideline.section: Low threshold for empirical treatment; test for gonorrhoea and chlamydia; exclude ectopic pregnancy; inpatient IV therapy for severe disease or tubo-ovarian abscess; partner notification
guideline.citation: Ross J, Cole M, Evans C, et al. United Kingdom national guideline for the management of pelvic inflammatory disease (2019 interim update). British Association for Sexual Health and HIV; 2019.

rationale: PID is a common mimic of appendicitis. Diagnosis is clinical; treatment is empirical antibiotics covering gonorrhoea, chlamydia and anaerobes, with STI testing and partner management.
